Rails parses with `Time.iso8601`; trails parses the same ISO 8601 string with `Temporal.Instant.from`.

Both branches are ported; Ruby's lenient `Time.parse` has no Temporal equivalent, so the non-standard-format branch parses with `new Date(...)` and converts to a `Temporal.Instant`, which is the same parse under a different call name.
Rails advances a `Time` with `Time.now.utc.advance(seconds:)`; trails' `Time` analogue is `Temporal.Instant`, whose equivalent is `add({ milliseconds })`.
